about: Venue truth table for UConn men's basketball 1986-87 to 2026-27. 'renames': each building's official names with effective date ranges (to = last day in effect; null = current); era name for a game = the names[] row whose from<=date<=to. 'home_site': per-game building for every app game flagged H plus every game actually played in Connecticut (or mislabeled as a Connecticut home site), resolved primarily from UConn's official Record Book (2026-27 ed.) per-game site codes (HCC/XL/PBA/GP/FH/WBA) and attendance, cross-checked against Wikipedia season tables, UConn's schedule archive, opponents' schedule archives, UConn game-notes box scores and AP datelines. Sports-Reference (sr_arena) and ESPN (espn_venue) proved unreliable for UConn home sites before 2006-07.

renames.building: Hartford arena (Hartford Civic Center / XL Center / PeoplesBank Arena), Hartford, CT

names.name: Hartford Civic Center
names.basis: opening (arena portion formally the Hartford Civic Center Veterans Memorial Coliseum); closed Jan 18, 1978 roof collapse - Feb 1980, same name

names.name: XL Center
names.basis: XL Insurance naming-rights deal announced the morning of 2007-12-18 and effective immediately ('the newly renamed venue'); UConn's contemporaneous box scores say 'Hartford Civic Center' for its 2007-12-16 game and 'XL Center' from its 2007-12-22 game on

names.name: PeoplesBank Arena
names.basis: 10-year PeoplesBank naming deal announced Monday 2025-06-02 ('It is now PeoplesBank Arena')

aliases: Hartford Civic Center Veterans Memorial Coliseum
renames.notes: The rename to XL Center was Dec 18, 2007, not October: UConn's official game notes print the box scores of its Nov 20, Nov 26 and Dec 16, 2007 games as 'Hartford Civic Center' and the Dec 22, 2007 game as 'XL Center' (UConn's current record book and Wikipedia season tables retroactively call the early-2007-08 games 'XL'). ESPN labels every Hartford game since 2003 'PeoplesBank Arena' (current name). UConn's last XL Center game was 2025-02-26; all 2025-26 games are PeoplesBank Arena. Arena closed for renovation summer 2025, reopened 2025-10-17.

renames.building: UConn Field House (now Hugh S. Greer Field House), Storrs, CT

names.name: University of Connecticut Field House
names.basis: opening (first game Dec 1, 1954 vs Rhode Island); commonly 'the Field House' / 'Storrs Field House'

names.name: Hugh S. Greer Field House
names.basis: UConn Board of Trustees voted to rename it for coach Hugh Greer 'a year' after basketball moved to Gampel in 1990 (exact vote date not found)

renames.notes: All UConn men's games here (last: Jan 24, 1990 vs Central Connecticut) predate the 1991 Greer naming, so the era-correct name is 'University of Connecticut Field House'; Sports-Reference's 'Hugh S. Greer Field House'/'UConn/Hugh S. Greer Fieldhouse'/'Storrs Field House' labels are anachronistic or informal. Now an indoor track facility.

renames.building: Downtown Omaha arena & convention center (Creighton home)

names.name: Qwest Center Omaha
names.basis: opening (Qwest bought 15-year, $14M naming rights before opening; official opening/first event per Wikipedia citing Omaha World-Herald 2003-09-20)

names.name: CenturyLink Center Omaha
names.basis: name change announced/adopted July 15, 2011 after CenturyLink's acquisition of Qwest (AP story datelined 2011-07-15); exterior signage physically replaced starting Sept 26, 2011

names.name: CHI Health Center Omaha
names.basis: effective date per 20-year, $23.6M naming-rights agreement announced 2018-06-20 ('As of September 1st, the building will be called the CHI Health Center Omaha')

aliases: Omaha Arena and Convention Center (construction name)
renames.notes: OPENING: 'opened' = 2003-09-20, the official opening/first event per Wikipedia (cites Omaha World-Herald 2003-09-20 'Roundup's new home has dirt welcome mat'). Other dates in circulation: a private Grand Funk Railroad concert on 2003-09-12 (Omaha World-Herald photo collection; Wikipedia infobox lists 2003-09-12 as 'inauguration'), and WOWT (2025 'Today in History') calls 2003-09-24 the first public event (River City Roundup Rodeo). The building was already 'Qwest Center Omaha' for all of these (name revealed ~5 weeks before opening per WOWT), so the choice does not affect any name lookup. Construction/planning name 'Omaha Arena and Convention Center' (a.k.a. Omaha Convention Center-Arena) is not included in names[]. CENTURYLINK (2011): Wikipedia gives July 15, 2011; an AP story 'Omaha's Qwest Center gets new name' on siouxcityjournal.com has an article ID whose embedded timestamp is 2011-07-15 (UTC), and Wikipedia also cites a Lincoln Journal Star story 'Qwest Center gets new name' dated 2011-07-16 (newspapers.com clip 176102230, not readable here). An older Wikipedia text (mirrored on en-academic.com) said July 22, 2011; the current article and the contemporaneous AP dating support July 15. The Qwest signs came down starting Monday Sept 26, 2011 (Omaha World-Herald photo caption; OWH 2011-09-27 'Qwest signs, logos making way for new name in town'), so venue signage still read Qwest until late Sept 2011 even though the official name had changed. SportsBusiness Journal (2011-03-24) reported all Qwest properties would transition to the CenturyLink name after the merger closed April 1, 2011. CHI HEALTH (2018): MECA announced the deal on Wednesday June 20, 2018 (WOWT, Pollstar, MECA press release PDF); all say the name became CHI Health Center Omaha effective September 1, 2018. SPECIFIC QUESTION - Sports-Reference labels for 2021-01-23 and 2022-03-02 ('CenturyLink Center Omaha') are STALE: both games were played after 2018-09-01, so the name in effect was CHI Health Center Omaha. All seven UConn games here (2021-2026) fall in the CHI Health Center Omaha era; no game is near a rename.
